友.meaning: You can't steer the boat alone: the <part>rudder</part> is too stiff. A second hand reaches over and grips it with yours, fingers twisted together like a <part>pretzel</part>. Two hands, one boat, one course. That's a <kanji>friend</kanji>.
友.on: Your friend gallops up on a <sound>u</sound>nicorn and offers to row the rest of the way.
友.kun: Your friend carves both your faces on a <sound>to</sound>tem pole and wraps its foot in a soft <sound>mo</sound>ccasin.

支.meaning: A tree's longest arm sags under its apples. A gardener's hand, twisted tight like a <part>pretzel</part>, wedges a crossed stick shaped like a <part>ten</part> underneath. Stick holds arm, arm holds apples: one <kanji>branch</kanji> propped up by another.
支.on: When the stick cracks, the gardener jams a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld under the branch instead.
支.kun: The propped branch holds a cat with a <sound>sa</sound>rdine in one paw and another <sound>sa</sound>rdine in the other, and it doesn't even bend.

持.meaning: A sailor leaves his <part>anchor</part> at the <part>temple</part> and asks a monk to mind it. The monk grips it in both arms all day, through prayers and lunch, never once setting it down. All he can do is <kanji>hold</kanji>.
持.on: At sunset the sailor rattles back in a muddy <sound>jee</sound>p, and the monk drops the anchor in the back.
持.kun: A <sound>mo</sound>ccasin slips off the monk's foot, dust tickles his nose, and he sneezes: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' Still he doesn't let go.

降.meaning: A climber plants her <part>pennant</part> on the summit, then unfolds a <part>folding chair</part> and rides it like a sled down a stone <part>staircase</part>, bump, bump, bump, all the way to the bottom. That's one way to <kanji>descend</kanji>.
降.on: At the bottom she's still clutching the ice cream <sound>co</sound>ne she bought at the top, now flat as a pancake.
降.kun: '<sound>Oh</sound>!' she yelps at every bump on the way down the stairs.

免.meaning: A kid sneaks out of class with a scarf <part>wrap</part>ped round his head, his <part>mouth</part> full of reasons and his <part>legs</part> already running. 'Dentist! Grandma! Dog ate my shoes!' The teacher just sighs at one more <kanji>excuse</kanji>.
免.on: He scribbled his excuse on the back of a café <sound>me</sound>nu, and the teacher reads it and gets hungry.
免.kun: '<sound>Ma</sound>, the <sound>noo</sound>k!' he whispers, and hides in a reading nook behind a bulb of <sound>ga</sound>rlic. Nobody finds him: he escapes.

晩.meaning: The <part>sun</part> sinks low, and a <part>rabbit</part> hops out of its burrow, ears up, nose twitching. It has waited all day for this: the sky going orange, then purple, then dark. Rabbit time is <kanji>nightfall</kanji>.
晩.on: The rabbit drags a sticky <sound>bun</sound> out of its burrow and nibbles it under the first stars.

飯.meaning: A plate of <part>food</part> sits in front of a kid who is firmly <part>anti</part> broccoli: arms crossed, mouth shut. Mum stands guard. Nobody leaves the table until it's eaten. It's the longest <kanji>meal</kanji> of the year.
飯.on: In the end Mum gives in and pours <sound>hon</sound>ey all over the broccoli.
飯.kun: Then a <sound>me</sound>ssy <sound>shee</sound>p wanders in from the garden and gobbles the broccoli off the plate.

院.meaning: A <part>pennant</part> flies over a building with <part>perfect</part> lawns, perfect windows, perfect rows of beds and staff in perfect white. Nothing here is ever out of place. It's an <kanji>institution</kanji>: a hospital, a school, a temple.
院.on: Everyone who comes in signs their name in <sound>in</sound>k in a huge book by the door.

病.meaning: A <part>leaky shed</part> drips on a traveller stuck in a <part>third class</part> bunk, the cheapest one, right under the hole. Drip, drip, all night long. By morning he's sneezing and shivering: <kanji>ill</kanji>.
病.on: Then a <sound>bee</sound> on a <sound>yo</sound>-yo drops through the hole and stings him on the nose, up and down, up and down.
病.kun: He shivers under a blanket knitted from one long ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn, still dripping wet.

心.meaning: A curved scoop lies on its side with a flick at one end, and three little drops jump above it: thump, thump, thump. Each drop is a beat, leaping out because it can't keep still. It's a <kanji>heart</kanji>, beating so hard it spills over.
心.on: Someone kicks you hard in the <sound>shin</sound>, and your heart starts to race.
心.kun: Your heart melts: a <sound>ko</sound>ala hugs a second <sound>ko</sound>ala, and a tiny <sound>ro</sound>dent hugs them both.

急.meaning: A <part>boomerang</part> comes whirling back straight at you. You drop your <part>rake</part> and run, <part>heart</part> pounding, leaves flying in every direction. No time to look back: <kanji>hurry</kanji>!
急.on: You dive under a pool table, and the boomerang snaps a pool <sound>cue</sound> clean in half.
急.kun: In your hurry you trip over an <sound>ee</sound>l asleep on the <sound>so</sound>fa.

特.meaning: Most cows graze in fields, but one <part>cow</part> lives at the <part>temple</part>, garlanded with flowers. Monks bow as it passes and feed it cakes by hand. It's no ordinary cow: it's <kanji>special</kanji>.
特.on: Even the temple clock goes tick-<sound>tock</sound> only when the special cow nods.

吐.meaning: A kid takes a big bite of a mud pie, and that <part>mouth</part> full of <part>soil</part> doesn't stay in long. Ptoo! Out it flies across the garden. There's only one thing to do: <kanji>spit</kanji>.
吐.on: The mud splats right across the face of the <sound>to</sound>tem pole.
吐.kun: '<sound>Ha</sound>!' he coughs, and spits the last bit of grit out of the garden shed door.

弟.meaning: At the goldfish's <part>funeral</part> in the garden, everyone stands quiet, except one small boy in a helmet with <part>horns</part>, who makes a <part>slash</part> through the air with a toy sword and declares the fish a hero. That's your <kanji>younger brother</kanji>.
弟.on: He seals the fish's matchbox coffin with a whole roll of sticky <sound>ta</sound>pe.
弟.kun: Your little brother drops a brick on your foot. '<sound>Oh</sound>! My <sound>toe</sound>!' you yell, hopping straight into the <sound>to</sound>tem pole.

里.meaning: A square rice field sits on top of a mound of good soil, the farm where you grew up. The field hasn't moved in fifty years, and Grandma still waves from the gate. It's your <kanji>hometown</kanji>.
里.on: Your hometown is a little fishing village beside a coral <sound>ree</sound>f.
里.kun: Back home, Grandma fries a <sound>sa</sound>rdine and props it against a <sound>to</sound>tem pole to cool.

理.meaning: A <part>king</part> visits a <part>farm</part> and asks why the crops grow in such neat rows. The farmer explains: sun here, water there, seeds in order. Every row has a reason. The king nods slowly: pure <kanji>logic</kanji>.
理.on: Back home, the king applies the same logic to his coral <sound>ree</sound>f and plants the fish in neat rows.
理.kun: The king's logic: a <sound>ko</sound>ala climbs, a <sound>to</sound>tem pole stands, a baby cries '<sound>Wah</sound>!', and fish live on a <sound>ree</sound>f.

動.meaning: A <part>heavy</part> piano blocks the hall. You flex every <part>muscle</part> you have, push, grunt, push again, and at last it slides one inch. It's not much, but you made it <kanji>move</kanji>.
動.on: Underneath the piano you find a squashed lump of bread <sound>dough</sound>.
動.kun: The piano rolls onto a bowl of <sound>u</sound>don, and noodles splash all over your swimming <sound>go</sound>ggles.

真.meaning: A <part>ten</part> sits on top of a <part>tool</part> rack: ten tools, ten tests. The jeweller scratches, weighs and squints at the diamond with every one of them, and it passes all ten. It's real. It's <kanji>true</kanji>.
真.on: For the last test, the jeweller taps the diamond on your <sound>shin</sound>. You yelp; it doesn't chip.
真.kun: The jeweller toasts the true diamond with a big <sound>mu</sound>g of tea.

業.meaning: On top, a row of <part>candles</part> burns late; under them a <part>sheep</part> shears its own wool, and the wool is knitted into hats on a <part>tree</part> stand below. Light, wool, hats, all night long: a family <kanji>business</kanji>.
業.on: Every hat the sheep sells comes with a free plate of <sound>gyo</sound>za.
業.kun: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' the crowd gasps at the ba<sound>za</sound>ar as the sheep knits a hat in ten seconds: a real skill.

九.meaning: A cat leaps: a <part>slash</part> of tail, then a <part>zigzag</part> of body that hooks up at the end. It has used up eight lives already, so it had better land well. This jump is number <kanji>nine</kanji>.
九.on: The cat lands on a pool table and skids the whole length of a pool <sound>cue</sound>.
九.kun: The cat counts the koalas in the tree, '<sound>Ko</sound>ala, <sound>ko</sound>ala…', and gives up at nine with a hiss: '<sound>No</sound>!'

熱.meaning: A <part>gardener</part> kneels to plant seeds, not knowing the bed is laid over <part>hot coals</part>. Steam curls up, his gloves smoke, and the seeds pop like popcorn. That soil is full of <kanji>heat</kanji>.
熱.on: He tries to fan the heat away with two fishing <sound>nets</sound>, and they melt.
熱.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' gasps the gardener, then sneezes in the steam: '<sound>Tsu</sound>!' His gloves are still smoking.

谷.meaning: At the top, two hills split apart like an <part>eight</part>; below them the slopes spread down like an open <part>umbrella</part>; and at the bottom a river <part>mouth</part> opens wide. Shout into it and it shouts back: a <kanji>valley</kanji>.
谷.on: A <sound>cock</sound>atoo shrieks back from the far side of the valley, louder than you.
谷.kun: Down in the valley a <sound>tu</sound>b floats along the river, with a sewing <sound>nee</sound>dle for a mast.

浴.meaning: <part>water drops</part> trickle down into a <part>valley</part> and pool in a steaming hot spring at the bottom. Monkeys and hikers climb in side by side. Everyone strips off to <kanji>bathe</kanji>.
浴.on: Someone cracks an egg into the spring, and the <sound>yolk</sound> cooks in a second.
浴.kun: '<sound>Ah</sound>!' sighs a monkey as it sinks into the hot water up to its ears.

至.meaning: A climber hooks an <part>elbow</part> over the last <part>one</part>-plank ledge, hauls herself up and plants her boots in the summit <part>soil</part>. The crowd far below roars. This is the moment the whole climb was for: the <kanji>climax</kanji>.
至.on: She raises a knight's <sound>shi</sound>eld over her head like a trophy.
至.kun: An <sound>ee</sound>l wriggles out of her pack and flops into a <sound>tu</sound>b of rainwater on the summit: it has arrived too.

室.meaning: Under a <part>roof</part>, a speaker climbs onto a <part>podium</part> and clears his throat. Everyone shuffles in, chairs scrape, the door clicks shut. Four walls, one speech: it's a <kanji>room</kanji>.
室.on: Halfway through, a bed <sound>shee</sound>t flaps down from the ceiling and covers the speaker.
室.kun: A <sound>moo</sound>se and a little <sound>ro</sound>dent sneak into the room and take the front row.

和.meaning: A farmer shares out sheaves of <part>grain</part> to every hungry <part>mouth</part> in the village. Nobody fights over the bread, nobody goes without. The whole place hums in <kanji>harmony</kanji>.
和.on: '<sound>Wah</sound>!' cries a baby who missed out, and stops the moment it's handed a crust.
和.kun: A ball of <sound>ya</sound>rn rolls over to the crying baby, and its '<sound>Wah</sound>!' softens into a giggle.

屋.meaning: A <part>flag</part> stretches across the top like an awning, sheltering a <part>podium</part> where a shopkeeper shouts out the day's prices. Rain drums on the cloth, but the stall stays dry under its <kanji>roof</kanji>.
屋.on: The shopkeeper is an <sound>oc</sound>topus, ringing up eight sales at once.
屋.kun: Today the stall sells nothing but <sound>ya</sound>rn, piled right up to the roof.

客.meaning: Under one <part>roof</part>, a host greets <part>each</part> visitor at the door with slippers and a cup of tea, one by one, until the hall is full. Every one of them is a <kanji>guest</kanji>.
客.on: One guest turns up late, paddling a ka<sound>yak</sound> right up to the front door.

洋.meaning: <part>water drops</part> splash over a <part>sheep</part> standing at the bow of a tiny boat, wool soaked, staring at waves to every horizon. It set off to find greener grass and found nothing but the <kanji>ocean</kanji>.
洋.on: Bored out at sea, the sheep plays with a <sound>yo</sound>-yo for weeks on end.

部.meaning: A <part>pennant</part> marks off each corner of the hall, and in every corner someone on a <part>soapbox</part> shouts about their own team: sales, tea, mail, paperclips. Each little corner is its own <kanji>section</kanji>.
部.on: Then a <sound>bu</sound>lldozer rolls in and shoves all the sections into one big pile.
部.kun: In the quietest section, someone has set up a <sound>be</sound>d and is fast asleep.
